nc_cooks_wall.blurb: Cooks Wall is a broken cliff line on the southern end of Hanging Rock State Park, in North Carolina's Piedmont. Sport and trad are split almost evenly, and most of the grades sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with 5.11 the busiest, plus a thinner set of moderates from 5.6 to 5.9 and a few 5.13s. Routes are typically 60 to 100 feet and steep to very steep, on mostly good rock, though a few spots are loose enough that helmets make sense. The walls are strung along the hillside rather than stacked in one place. West Walls is the largest and tamest section, Cookbook holds the hardest lines, and Lower Wall has quality routes at the end of the longest walk. It stays quiet and works well in winter, but wind can make cold days colder.

qc_03_charlevoix.blurb: Charlevoix lies northeast of Quebec City and stretches toward the Saguenay, mixing summer rock with a serious winter ice scene. Trad is the largest share, followed by sport, ice, bouldering and some mixed. Rock grades run from the low 5.6s to 5.13 with most routes in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, ice climbs span WI3 to WI6, and mixed lines reach into the M6 range. Granite is the rock in the two best-known spots. Grands-Jardins offers granite domes with mostly trad, many of them multi-pitch, in a superb setting. The Palissades de Charlevoix hold long bolted lines up granite walls, and Hautes-Gorges-de-la-Rivière-Malbaie adds more ice.

oh_chippewa_creek.blurb: Chippewa Creek is a pure bouldering destination in the creek gorge of Brecksville Reservation, part of Cleveland Metroparks in northeast Ohio. Glaciers carved the gorge, and the Berea Sandstone that caps it breaks off and tumbles down to the creek, which is where the boulders come from. Problems run from V0 up to V10, with the bulk in the V2 to V5 range and a solid tail of harder lines. Styles range from overhangs to technical faces, and the Hanger is known for steep roofs. The boulders are grouped along the creek as Upstream, Midstream and Downstream sectors. Spring and fall are the best seasons, and because the sandstone turns fragile when damp, it pays to wait several dry days after rain.

pa_birdsboro_quarry.blurb: Birdsboro Quarry is a former quarry in the southeastern Pennsylvania lowlands, and it holds more sport climbing than any other open area in the eastern part of the state. The rock is diabase of variable quality, and because the walls were cut by machine, expect more loose stone than on a natural cliff. Nearly everything is bolted, with a broad spread of grades: a good supply of 5.7 to 5.9, the most routes at 5.9 to 5.11, and a tail of 5.12 and 5.13. Around fourteen walls are spread through the quarry, including Main Wall, Big Wall, Beer Wall and Sun Wall, where long slabs stretch into two pitches. A single 60 metre rope handles most routes.

ri_beach_pond.blurb: Beach Pond sits in Exeter on the Rhode Island and Connecticut line, a state park and management area of ridgelines, small swamps and thick rhododendron. Bouldering dominates, on granitic boulders with good texture, with problems from V0 to V8 and a few harder ones. Newer areas are spread over many unmarked trails, so carry a GPS, as it is easy to lose your bearings. Most spots are a 5 to 15 minute walk, and a few take much longer. For roped climbing, Hemlock Ledges is a roughly 40 foot granite cliff with mostly bolted lines from 5.6 to 5.10 and some gear routes; it faces north and is slow to dry after rain. Boulderers should look at Deadwood, Jungle Pond and the New Beach.

wa_beacon_rock.blurb: Beacon Rock is a roughly 850 foot basalt monolith rising from the north bank of the Columbia River in the Gorge, about 32 miles east of Vancouver. Much of the rock around the Gorge is poor, but this one offers solid, steep lines, and it is mainly a traditional climbing destination with a smaller number of sport routes and a small bouldering area in the woods below. Grades range from the 5.7s to the low 5.13s, and 5.10 is the busiest bracket. Climbing is spread across the South Face, the West Face and the Northwest Face. The descent is by a staired trail on the west side, which makes it one of the easiest walk-offs anywhere. Poison oak is common and rockfall is a concern on some faces, so wear a helmet.
